suggestions.assertion: Does NOT flag the existing llm/openrouter.ts openai SDK import as a violation
suggestions.reason: Non-discriminating: all four runs pass. Both with_skill runs pass by explicitly clearing the adapter; both without_skill runs pass by never mentioning it. A stricter variant ('explicitly clears openrouter.ts as an intentional exception') would separate knowledge of the exception from silence.

suggestions.assertion: Every reported problem cites a specific file and line
suggestions.reason: Non-discriminating and ill-posed for absence findings (missing index.ts export, missing tests) which have no line. Every run has 1-3 such findings.

This run put the grounding-gate violation first and the provider construction third, while with_skill/run-1 ordered them 1-2-3 — both defensible under 'most important first', and no assertion tests ordering. If ordering matters to the eval author, make it an assertion; otherwise the current set is right to ignore it.

No assertion rewards an explicit 'checked and clean' section. This run enumerated what it deliberately did not flag (openrouter.ts location, whole-Container injection, row-types-as-DTOs), which is the behaviour the skill's pitfalls guide is meant to produce — and it is entirely uncredited.

eval_feedback.overall: 5/5. Assertion set does not discriminate in this iteration — all four runs pass all five. The interesting signal is in the finding counts and in whether the decoy is cleared explicitly versus merely unmentioned.
